newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Products Outlook-Distillates' rally falters.
newsitem.headline: Asia Products Outlook-Distillates' rally falters.

text.p: Light and middle distillates attempted a recovery in short-lived bull runs last week, but traders on Monday expected fundamentals to improve with Asia heading into the fourth quarter.
The gas oil market traded some 1.1 million barrels, chalking up a rise of $1.85 per barrel until Thursday when a European major emerged to sell physical cargoes.

Traders said the latest price was also due to a surge in swap values after some financial houses and East-West spread players came out to buy the front month, and aggravated by traders forced to buy to cover earlier short sales.
But with the recent short-covering to Indonesia, the destination for most of last week's purchases, traders were expecting a price correction over the next week.
"The market was on a strong bull run because there were no sellers and until the major came out people were not convinced that fundamentally this market is long," one trader said.
Singapore's Trade Development Board which showed that middle distillate stocks for the week ending July 23 rose by 469,000 barrels to a high of 11.084 million.
Some traders said stocks in China also remained high and it was not likely to import large amounts in the near future.

But others hoped that China would finally emerge to buy diesel for September or late August delivery after it halved its monthly purchases in the second quarter and probably in the third quarter as well, from more than two million tonnes in the first quarter.

Traders were also bullish in their outlook as the region heads into the fourth quarter, the traditional peak period for middle distillates as north Asian refiners begin stockpiling for the winter season.
Japanese and South Korean refiners are also expected to switch production to maximise middle distillates.
"Middle distillate stocks in Japan and South Korea are very high and refiners are producing more light distillates," a South Korean refiner said. "(Naphtha) Supplies are greater than requirements."
Japanese refiners have been running more light crude and their naphtha ouput in April and May jumped 20 percent from a year ago, refiners said.

The backwardation seen in the Asian naphtha market since July 10 disappeared early last week, amid slack regional demand and no sign of the re-emergence of the heavy Thai buying which had soaked up the excess prompt cargoes.
"If you look at the factors, there are no bullish factors but so many bearish ones," said a trader with a major oil company. "Naphtha was being driven up by the open-spec buyers."
"The market is directionless," said a trader.

"It should head back into backwardation as the market heads into prepartion for winter and Japanese and South Korean refiners focus their operations on middle distillate production instead on the light ends," he said. "But fundamentally, I don't see it in a deep backwardation."
High octane gasoline started to rally amid tight supplies, partially due to cuts in reforming capacity in the region and firm octane enhancer MTBE prices.
In the absence of sellers, a European major raised his bid for early August supplies of 97-octane unleaded gasoline since Wednesday, raised its bid by $1.20 per barrel to $25.50, fob Singapore.

High sulphur fuel oil traded firmer at $95 per tonne for the 380-cst grade and $98 for 180-cst, with buyers still seeking supplies, while suppliers stayed on the sidelines, waiting for higher bids, traders said.
Continued buying interest supported market sentiment but traders said they did not expect significant gains in the near term despite a fall in the Singapore weekly residues.
The Singapore weekly fuel oil residues stocks registered a fall of 860,000 barrels to 11.074 million barrels in the week ending July 23.
"The stocks level shows that supplies are still sufficient at the moment," said one trader.

In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, traders were awaiting Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina to annouce its August allocation, which is expected to be higher than July's initial allocation of 2.3 million barrels.
"Sentiment is not as firm as earlier this month though prices should be still well supported at above $16.00 per barrel," said one trader.
